english_verification.review_scope: Cross-checked the original main JSON national_ideas idea.text_en values against current Mod English localization, the country and adjective, L62 national-idea names/text, selected ruler names, Harimari migration context, and representative slave-sale gating and shortage effects; this is not a full source-code audit. unresolved: The offline English Wiki result is demographic context only, not a Vandipha country page; it does not verify mission mechanics, all national-idea effects, values scores, or hands-on difficulty.

rationale.campaign_length: 36 directly defined missions, extending across several sea regions; this is a structural-catalogue count, not a mission-by-mission audit.
rationale.colonization: Island and overseas-port expansion are important; not every conquest is classified as colonization.
rationale.complexity: Naval and land projection, the sale cycle, subject relations, and port management must be coordinated.
rationale.dark_story: The sale of enslaved people, labor under the lash, and obligations to supply slaves are central to the narrative.
rationale.difficulty: Managing several threads and projecting overseas add operational burden; player-strength claims are not used as balance conclusions.
rationale.diplomacy: Buyers, Harimari-subject opinion and gifts, and the trade network all have explicit requirements.
rationale.early_pressure: Navy and finances, regional rivals, and several diplomatic thresholds; difficulty has not been playtested.
rationale.magic_artifice_intensity: The verified core is maritime trade, enslavement, and naval power; there is no unique spellcasting or artificery loop. High Philosophy does not automatically imply magical power.
rationale.narrative_density: Island trade, the slave city, subject integration, and overseas cultural expansion form a connected main arc.
rationale.tall_play: Capital defenses, courts, conscription facilities, and the palace must be developed alongside foreign operations.
rationale.trade_economy: Slave sales, triangular trade, and several charter-company regions form the core loop.
rationale.warfare: Regional expansion and naval projection drive the route; it is not a purely land-based unification campaign.

identity.appearance: In 1444, a Roaming Harimari coastal island nation following High Philosophy and the Starry Eye school, beginning as a monarchy. Local English country key: Vandipha (L62); English adjective: Vandiphan.
identity.formation_scope: The verified unique mission and event route remains with L62; no unique tag-changing formable has been confirmed. Generic formation decisions are not promised as this article's sequel.
identity.region: East Sarhal coast / island in the Gulf of Rahen

national_ideas.scope_note: National tradition, seven national ideas, and ambition; excludes optional idea groups and racial/government bonuses. Multiple candidates and their conditions are listed separately and are not treated as simultaneous; whether new ideas are accepted upon formation depends on the actual event/decision and player choice.

description.text: To many harimari we are the first stop on a journey into Sarhal or the penultimate one coming from Yanshen. During their stopover they wonder at our serene beaches, our primal jungles, or our royal abodes as they peek out from beyond the teak trees. Our island of Van has thus earned a reputation as a place of unusual luxury, where even the lowest of the low can become their own master. Because of this way of living, which few other harimari kingdoms can match, we try to exert considerable influence on those that pass near. We offer glory, chattel or beach-front land, or less tangible things like wisdom from outside the High Temples or outlets for their considerable martial skill in our navy. Taking on such recruits helps us maintain our island's way of life against the various pirates and Raghamideshi merchants that surround us.

description.text: We seldom get our paws dirty with the actual task of catching and controlling chattel, preferring to leave it to the slavers guild. Nevertheless, many slaves pass through our lands, whether they be mundane humans from Rahen or more exotic lizardfolk from beyond the Baashidi. With this constant coming and going of slaves, a great many ideas are passed from them to us. Often, the slaves bought for our own use end up being used as tutors, servants, and advisors, all with their own ideas of how the world works. This adds to our greater understanding of the High Gods, as even within a slave is a fragment of that knowledge.

description.text: Among the Roaming Harimari there is a tradition when one comes of age to travel to a foreign kingdom and live amongst its people for a year. Upon one’s return, one is to dye multiple stripes in one’s fur of a color representing the region one went to. From then on, any time they go to a new region it is expected for them to dye a further single stripe; some of the most-traveled thus become almost kaleidoscopic. In our kingdom we add an addendum to this tradition. When a warrior touches an enemy in battle and lives to tell the tale, they are allowed to paint golden stripes on their face in the shape of a horned devil. Not only does this show they are to be feared, it also shows other harimari that the wearer has completed a second coming-of-age, one that proves they are old enough to fight.

description.text: Our proximity to the Sarhali main means that Mengi people have long come to Van to trade and settle. As the Baashidi have come to be more involved in trade in the gulf, they too have sought out our island. With these two different peoples coming into close contact, some even living on the island and joining the slavers guild, we began to notice similarities between their beliefs and our own. We agree on the place where divinity resides, the sky, and we agree that these divine sky beings send out messages for mortals to follow and interpret, whether that be weather, sun or stars. These convergent beliefs have led to a new creed, the Rainbow Dawn, which argues that enlightenment lies not just in the High Temples but in all nature around us, and is discernible by all through empirical study. Though this philosophy is small and only those not in power on the island follow it, it has led many to take greater note of our surroundings and cultivate a greater understanding of our natural world.

description.text: In the largest settlement of the island sits the Matak Payar or Pearl Bazaar. Its builder took inspiration from his own travels, adorning the bazaar with Bulwari minarets, Raheni vimanas, and Bom Statues. It is adorned with a veritable menagerie of materials: ebony from the Mengi, jade from the Yan, marble from Tamran owned hills, and 10,001 local pearls arranged in a mandala. Over half of the island’s slave trade occurs here, and within its arcade sits the headquarters of the slavers guild, in which various foreigners process, manage, capture, buy and sell slaves. Its exquisite beauty and hybrid style show off how far our people have traveled and help to bring in trade to the island.

Various ships all sail within the Rahen Gulf and Ringlet Sea. Be it Junks from Yanshen, Gatawian canoes, Ofehibi iron hulls, or Baashidi style sunchasers, at one point or another all of these ships have called our ports home. From here we have developed a new style of ship building, combining design features from each of these fleets. These Umsadapti ‘sea lords’ allow us to board larger crews and absorb more cannon fire, without sacrificing maneuverability. These ships are too heavy for the open oceans, but have allowed us to force pirates out of their hideouts and into watery exile.

description.text: As the slave trade in Rahen entered its second twilight, with the rise of the Praxis and Suhan’s message that a slave could eventually find his freedom through their actions, many on Van took this message further. Over time, two camps on Van formed; those who supported the continuation of slavery, wearing a pearl ring on their claw in support of the ruling family, and those opposed, often wearing an amulet of a Dakinshi supposedly praying to the High Gods.The situation eventually boiled over into a civil war which saw huge losses, only for it to end in disappointment for all sides. Bhuvauri, seeing the instability of one of its more prominent suppliers, felt that if the island were to give up slavery it would represent a great loss. Initially they supported the pearl-ringed, but over time they overthrew the king to take direct control. While this initially led to rings making greater headway against the amulets, eventually the two forces would begrudgingly put their differences aside in order to fight off Bhuvauri.

player_overview.avoid_if: You cannot accept a slave-trade main storyline, or want only continuous land warfare without managing fleets and diplomatic relations.
player_overview.how_it_plays: First secure the island and sea routes, then manage slave transactions and subject relations, and finally use naval protection to expand ports across the ocean.
player_overview.overview: Vandipha is a Harimari island nation off eastern Sarhal that grew through maritime commerce linking inland supply with buyers in Rahen. You must build a fleet and protect the market while maintaining relations with Harimari subjects, then extend the port network to distant shores. The defining mechanic is the sale of enslaved people: different buyers and the self-purchase option have different rewards. The country builds cities while using forced labor to support prosperity; limited acts of liberation do not mean the state has left the slave trade.
player_overview.recommended_for: Players who enjoy naval power, trade networks, subject management, and dark commercial narratives.
signature_features: Slave sales connect buyer choices with money and national rewards.
A Harimari subject network and maritime ports jointly support commercial control.
The trade network eventually reaches Haless, turning port influence into Harimari cultural expansion.
player_overview.tagline: Use a navy, ports, and a subject network to turn Vandipha into a transoceanic slave-trade empire.

positive_indicators: Coastal defense, courts, and port construction
Mission effects reduce the enslaved gnoll population and increase tolerance
Actions exist to reduce the enslavement of some groups, but this is not equivalent to abolition
values.rationale: Slave sales, labor under the lash in slave cities, and subject obligations to supply enslaved people are clear violations of personhood and cannot be offset by maritime prosperity. Coastal defense, courts, ports, and mission effects reducing the enslavement of gnolls provide limited public benefit. Cultural conversion is primarily reflected on the pluralism axis and is not deducted again from the values score; war, imperialization, monarchy, and trade monopolies do not themselves incur deductions. Dynamic population modifiers are not expanded into a claim of extermination, and the title Liberator of Humans is not treated as proof of general abolition. Compared with anchors Rósande 22, Corvuria 23, and Deranne 6, the route retains enslavement at its core while including construction and limited mitigation; evidence does not establish more severe commodification of populations. No stage improvement of 20 points or more has been established, so the trajectory is stable. Confidence is medium because this has not been verified in hands-on play.
red_flags: Treating sapient beings as enslaved people who can be sold or purchased for domestic use
Slave cities run on forced labor and the lash
The Harimari subject relationship makes supplying slaves an obligation
